name: Sinclair Broadcast Group

summary.text: Sinclair Broadcast Group is a Maryland-based owner of local television stations, reported in 2018 to be the largest local TV station owner in the United States with about 173 stations. In March 2018 its news chief directed stations to have anchors read an identical promotional script warning about "fake stories" and media bias; a Deadspin montage of dozens of anchors reciting it went viral in April 2018. Sinclair also required stations to air "must-run" commentary segments, including those of chief political analyst Boris Epshteyn, which it ended in December 2019. In May 2020 Sinclair agreed to pay a $48 million civil penalty to the FCC, the largest in the agency's history for a broadcaster, resolving inquiries connected to its failed $3.9 billion acquisition of Tribune Media.

facts.claim: In March 2018 Sinclair's news chief, Scott Livingston, directed stations to have anchors read a script about "fake stories" and "personal bias" in the media, according to a memo obtained by CNNMoney; Deadspin then published a video of dozens of Sinclair anchors reciting the same speech, including the line "This is extremely dangerous to our democracy."
facts.quote: Deadspin then published a video showing dozens of TV anchors from Sinclair Broadcast Group reciting the same speech warning against "biased and false news."

facts.claim: Sinclair defended the promotional script; Livingston said it was "a warning about fake news circulating on social media."
facts.quote: Livingston said the news anchor script is "a warning about fake news circulating on social media."

facts.claim: A 2018 report put Sinclair's holdings at 173 television stations, with its commentaries airing on 84 stations that produce local news.
facts.quote: A Little Village report from the period put its total at 173 TV stations, and its commentaries appeared on 84 stations that air local news.

facts.claim: In 2018 Sinclair tripled the frequency of "must-run" segments by its chief political analyst Boris Epshteyn, a former Trump aide, from three times a week; stations had no discretion over must-run content, which also included segments from Mark Hyman and the "Terrorism Alert Desk."
facts.quote: his "Bottom Line with Boris" segments already aired three times a week, but would now triple in frequency

facts.claim: In December 2019 Sinclair ended its political commentary segments featuring Epshteyn and another analyst, saying it would move toward investigative journalism and allot the airtime to additional storytelling, with the segments ending Friday, December 13.
facts.quote: The company's statement explained that it would allot the airtime to additional storytelling, ending the commentary segments that Friday, Dec. 13.

facts.claim: On May 6, 2020, Sinclair agreed to pay a $48 million civil penalty under an FCC consent decree, which the FCC described as the largest civil penalty paid by a broadcaster in the agency's history. The decree resolved three inquiries: Sinclair's disclosure of material information in its proposed acquisition of Tribune Media stations, whether it negotiated retransmission consent agreements in good faith, and its failure to identify the sponsor of content it produced and supplied to television stations.
facts.quote: the penalty was the largest civil penalty paid by a broadcaster in the agency's history.
